Create a comprehensive personal finance application called "Indian Money Code" using Next.js (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and ShadCN UI components.

1. Core App Structure & Styling:

Layout: Create a main application layout (src/app/(main)/layout.tsx) with a collapsible sidebar for navigation and a header containing a user profile dropdown menu. Authentication pages (/login, /signup, etc.) should have a separate, simpler centered layout (src/app/(auth)/layout.tsx).
Styling: Configure src/app/globals.css to use a dark theme with the following HSL color variables:
--background: 222 47% 11% (Dark Gray)
--primary: 243 80% 58% (Indigo)
--accent: 244 86% 66% (Purple)
Font: Use the 'Inter' sans-serif font across the application.
Icons: Use the lucide-react library for all icons.
2. Firebase Integration & Data Management:

Authentication: Implement user authentication using Firebase Authentication with the Email/Password provider. This includes creating pages for Sign Up, Login, Forgot Password, and Email Verification.
Firestore Database: Use Firestore to store user-specific data. The database structure must enforce strict user ownership using a top-level users collection, where all user data is stored in subcollections under /users/{userId}. Create subcollections for investments, goals, insurances, budget (for categories), and transactions.
Robust Provider: Create a single, unified AppProvider (src/context/AppProvider.tsx). This provider is critical and must handle the following in a sequential and robust manner to prevent race conditions:
Initialize Firebase safely on the client-side only (using useEffect).
Manage the user's authentication state using onAuthStateChanged.
Handle all application routing: redirect unauthenticated users to /login, and redirect authenticated users from auth pages to /dashboard. It should also handle the /verify-email page logic.
Fetch all user data from Firestore (investments, goals, etc.) only after confirming the user is authenticated.
Provide the Firebase services (auth, firestore) and all fetched data to the entire application via a single context. While initializing and fetching, a full-page loading indicator should be displayed.
3. Feature Implementation (Pages & Components):

Dashboard (/dashboard): Display a "Welcome Back" message. Include a high-level summary of the user's net worth (calculated from investments) and cards that link to other key features like Portfolio, Goals, and Projections.
Budget (/budget):
Display summary cards for Total Income, Total Budgeted, Total Spent, and Savings.
Allow users to create and manage budget categories with allocated amounts (e.g., "Food", "Transportation"). Show progress bars for each category.
Include a form to log new transactions (expenses) and income.
Show a breakdown of spending by category using a recharts Pie Chart.
List recent transactions.
Goals (/goals):
Allow users to create, view, and delete financial goals (e.g., "House Down Payment," "Retirement").
Each goal should have a name, target amount, and target date.
Display progress towards each goal, calculated from the currentValue of linked investments.
Portfolio (/portfolio):
Implement a tabbed interface for "Investments" and "Insurance".
Investments Tab:
Display summary cards for total invested value, current value, and overall profit/loss.
Allow users to perform CRUD operations on their investments (e.g., Stocks, Mutual Funds). Each investment must be linked to a goal.
Include an "Import from CSV" feature.
Insurance Tab:
Allow users to perform CRUD operations on their insurance policies (e.g., Life, Health). Each policy should have details like coverage, premium, and expiry date.
Loans (/loans): Create a page to manage and track various loans (Personal, Home, Car, etc.). Include a loan prepayment simulator to calculate interest savings and tenure reduction.
Projections (/projections): Create a wealth projection page with a recharts Line Chart. Allow users to simulate their future wealth based on current portfolio value, monthly investments, and expected annual return.
Calculators (/calculators): Create a page with a tabbed interface for various financial calculators: SIP, Lump Sum, EMI, Inflation, FIRE, SWP, etc.
Profile (/profile): A page where users can view their email and update their display name.
4. AI-Powered Features (using Genkit and Gemini):

AI Portfolio Summary: On the portfolio page, add an "Analyze with AI" button that uses a Genkit flow (summarizeInvestmentPortfolio) to analyze the user's investment data (passed as a JSON string) and return a text summary of portfolio health, diversification, and suggestions.
AI Will Generator (/will-generator): Create a form where a user can input their details (name, address, executor, beneficiaries, assets, etc.). Use a Genkit flow (generateWill) to generate a draft Last Will and Testament document based on the input. Include a clear legal disclaimer.
Voice Transaction Logging: On the budget page, add a "Log with Voice" feature. It should use the browser's microphone to record the user's voice, send the audio data URI to a Genkit flow (logTransactionFromAudio), and use the returned structured data (description, amount, category) to log the transaction.
